source: NCERT Class XII, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 2), Ch. 3 (The Mughal School of Miniature Painting).

sections.heading: 1. Origins of Mughal Painting
points: The **Mughal school** blended **Persian, Indian and (later) European** styles into a distinctive court art.
It began under **Humayun**, who brought Persian masters **Mir Sayyid Ali and Abd-us-Samad** to India.
It reached its height under **Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan**; declined under Aurangzeb (who discouraged painting).

sections.heading: 2. Akbar's Reign
points: **Akbar** established a large **imperial atelier (karkhana)**; illustrated great manuscripts: the **Hamzanama (Dastan-i-Amir Hamza), Akbarnama, Razmnama (Persian Mahabharata)**.
Style: **vigorous, colourful, crowded compositions**, blending Persian finesse with Indian vitality.
Artists: **Daswanth, Basawan, Miskin**; painting was a **collaborative** effort (design, colour, portrait done by different artists).

sections.heading: 3. Jahangir and Shah Jahan
points: **Jahangir** — a great connoisseur; emphasis on **naturalism, portraiture, and studies of birds, animals and flowers**; masters like **Ustad Mansur** (natural history — the dodo, the Siberian crane), **Abul Hasan, Bishandas**.
Fine **borders (hashiya)**, **allegorical portraits** (Jahangir preferring a Sufi to kings) reflect European influence.
**Shah Jahan** — more **formal, jewel-like, refined** painting; court scenes and portraits; use of gold; the tradition became more decorative.

sections.heading: 4. Techniques and Legacy
points: Techniques: **fine brushwork, shading, perspective (from European art), rich mineral colours, gold**.
Mughal painting influenced **Rajasthani, Deccan and Pahari** schools.
After Aurangzeb, court artists dispersed to regional courts, spreading the style.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Mughal painting began under Humayun (Persian masters Mir Sayyid Ali, Abd-us-Samad).
Akbar: Hamzanama, Akbarnama, Razmnama; artists Daswanth, Basawan.
Jahangir: naturalism, portraiture; Ustad Mansur (birds/animals — dodo, Siberian crane).
Shah Jahan: formal, refined, jewel-like painting.
Aurangzeb discouraged painting → artists dispersed to regional courts.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Mughal painting began under Humayun** (not Babur); flourished under Akbar-Jahangir-Shah Jahan.
**Ustad Mansur (Jahangir's court)** specialised in **birds, animals and flowers** (dodo, Siberian crane).
**Akbar commissioned the Hamzanama, Akbarnama and Razmnama**.
**Aurangzeb discouraged** painting, causing artists to migrate to regional courts.
